proposals.evidence: DEDR4449 gives the widespread southern pēn/pēnu louse family, including Kannada pēn, Malayalam pēn and Telugu pēnu. These survey pyānu/pēnə/yɛ̄ñu/ēnu forms retain the louse stem with ordinary final vowels or Kannada-area initial weakening; survey palatalization is preserved. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR183 explicitly gives Irula amme father, Tulu amme father and Gondi amma/ammal father within the amma kin-term family. Betta Kurumba amman and Urali ammɛ father compare with that attested paternal use; the source father gloss is preserved rather than changed to mother. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
